subject: Microtable renewal: capacity restructure + temporary rate hold request
messages:
From: Alex Warren <alex@microtable.io>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@microtable.io
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal discussion — spike in Q4 and pricing ask

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the check-in last week. Quick recap from our side: Microtable is preparing for a product launch in Q4 that will temporarily increase inference usage ~3-4x for 8-10 weeks. We love Redwood's performance but the current committed model doesn't fit the short spike — procurement is worried about overage exposure.

Two asks from our finance/ops team:
- A temporary rate-hold at our current blended price for 90 days during the spike (no automatic step-up on projected usage), and
- A one-time credit to cover measured overage for that period (we're proposing a $25k safety credit applied to invoices after the quarter).

We are ready to sign a 12-month renewal today if we can align on those two items and a modest uplift to committed capacity after the spike (we'd increase from 6 to 12 reserved units).

Can you share what flexibility Redwood has on a short-term rate-hold and temporary credit? Happy to set a short call with procurement if helpful.

— Alex
Head of Ops, Microtable

P.S. attaching our June/July usage export for context (summary attached).

From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Alex Warren <alex@microtable.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — spike in Q4 and pricing ask

Alex — thanks for the clear context and the usage file. Really excited about Microtable's launch. Short answers up front: yes, we can do a timebound rate-hold paired with capacity uplift, but we need to align on the true-up mechanics and a clear termination/roll-back condition.

High-level proposal from Redwood:
- 90-day temporary rate-hold at your existing blended rate starting on first spike day.
- One-time safety credit of $20k applied to the invoice immediately following the spike quarter (we can carve additional credits for committed upsell).
- Post-spike: auto-true-up on actual consumption vs. committed uplift; if you commit to bump reserved units from 6 to 12 for the remaining term, we can split the cost of the credit (Redwood covers $12.5k, Microtable covers $12.5k).
- Legal: we will include a simple amendment (SOW addendum) with the window, credit amount, and clear definitions of "spike window" and "baseline".

Next steps I suggest: 1) I'll loop in pricing to confirm the credit split and 2) Marissa can draft the amendment so procurement can review. If procurement needs tighter guarantees, we can consider an invoice holdback structure.

Would a call tomorrow at 10am PT work to align?

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Senior AM, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Alex Warren <alex@microtable.io>, chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — SOW addendum and proposed terms

Alex — following Chloe's note, attaching a first-pass SOW addendum for the temporary rate-hold and capacity uplift. Key clauses called out in the doc:

- Term window: defined start and end dates for the 90-day hold; activation tied to a usage threshold (e.g., sustained 48-hour >2.5x baseline) to avoid accidental activation.
- Credit mechanics: safety credit to be invoiced as a negative line item after the quarter close; credit applied only to customer invoices, non-refundable.
- Commit change: optional commitment to increase reserved units to 12 after the spike; includes prorated billing and a 30-day notice to revert to previous levels.
- True-up & reporting: both parties will use agreed usage export (CSV) for reconciliation; Redwood reserves right to audit usage with 7 days' notice.

Attachment: SOW-draft-20260830.pdf (SOW addendum — redlines included).

If that looks close, I'll send to procurement with a DocuSign-ready version. If procurement is pushing for the full $25k credit, we can present the split option (Redwood matches 50% if they sign the 12-month renewal with the uplift).

— Marissa
Director, Renewals Operations
Redwood Inference

From: procurement@microtable.io
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Warren <alex@microtable.io>
Date: 2026-09-01T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — procurement feedback on SOW addendum

Hi Marissa/Chloe,

Procurement reviewed the SOW addendum. Two items we need clarified before we route to finance:
1) "Activation threshold": can you confirm the exact metric and how the 48-hour sustained condition is measured? We need a deterministic trigger.
2) "Credit application": we require the safety credit to be visible on the invoice and applied before late fee calculations — and we request a 45-day payment term for the invoice that the credit will reduce.

Also, Microtable prefers the $25k credit you outlined initially. In return, we will commit to the 12 reserved units for the next 9 months (instead of 12) and agree to a short performance SLA addendum for the spike window.

If those points look feasible, we can sign by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Microtable Procurement Team

From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: procurement@microtable.io, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Warren <alex@microtable.io>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-02T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — final alignment and next steps

Procurement — appreciate the clear asks. Confirmations below:

1) Activation threshold: the spike window will activate when observed 48-hour rolling average token consumption exceeds 250% of the baseline (baseline = average daily token usage over the trailing 60 days prior to activation). Redline in the SOW will include the exact formula and an automated measurement report retained for audit.

2) Credit application and payment term: we will show the $25,000 safety credit as a negative line on the invoice after quarter close and will honor a 45-day payment term on that invoice. Redwood's finance is on board with that flow.

Regarding the credit amount: Redwood will accept the $25k credit split option — Redwood will cover $12.5k if Microtable signs the 9-month 12-unit reserved commitment (as procurement proposed). If Microtable prefers the full $25k on Redwood alone, we would need to extend the committed term to 18 months to cover the economics.

Next steps:
- Marissa will produce a DocuSign-ready addendum reflecting the activation metric, credit line, 45-day term, and 9-month 12-unit commitment with the 50/50 credit split.
- Ben and David will prepare a short technical appendix describing how KV caching and autoscaling will be configured during the spike.
- Target: EOD Friday signature to meet procurement timeline.

I'll attach updated SOW and push DocuSign link once Marissa confirms. Thanks all — moving fast on this is great.

Best,
Chloe
